summary: 'What is your name' in ASL is YOU NAME WHAT, with the eyebrows down on WHAT. Three signs, no 'is.'
steps: Sign NAME: two H handshapes, the top one tapping twice on the bottom.
Sign WHAT with lowered eyebrows and hold the face until they answer.
note: The question word comes last in ASL. English order (WHAT YOUR NAME) is understood but marks you as a beginner. Practice ending on WHAT with the eyebrows down.
mistakes: Raised eyebrows. That turns it into 'is that your name?'
Signing YOUR (flat hand) instead of YOU (point). Both are heard, but YOU NAME WHAT is the common form.
